title: Credit Arbitration & Soft-Shepherd Tier Router with Predictive Degradation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Free, paid, and enterprise plans compete for limited serving capacity across regions. Under load we need a graceful, quota-aware admission policy that: (1) protects enterprise/paid commitments, (2) avoids hard failures for free users where possible, and (3) selects lowest-cost compatible model variants and regions automatically.

Goal: Implement a Credit Arbitration service and Soft-Shepherd routing layer that performs per-request prioritization using a small token escrow, predictive short-term smoothing (for bursty tenants), and progressive degradation to lower-cost model variants and/or remote regions when local capacity or plan credits are low. The system should prefer preserving latency SLOs for higher tiers while giving free tier requests a chance via conservative prefetching/fallbacks rather than immediate 403s.

Non-goals: Full multi-tenant fairness research, billing policy changes, or replacing existing quota accounting. This ticket focuses on runtime admission and routing decisions only.
acceptance_criteria: Credit Arbitration service returns admission decisions within 500µs P95 in steady state
Requests are routed to a fallback model variant (quantized or smaller) for >= 90% of simulated free-tier credit-exhaustion bursts instead of being dropped
Enterprise-tier requests have <1% increased latency from baseline under mixed load (validated in perf test harness)
Canary rollout across a single region with toggle via Console and automatic rollback on error rate >1%
End-to-end observability: per-request decision reason (admit/soft-demote/fail), credit delta, chosen model variant, and route region appear in request trace and dashboard
technical_design:
High-level architecture: (1) credit-arbiter microservice that ingests plan credit state (from billing/quotas cache) and short-term smoothing signals (moving average of recent consumption), (2) soft-shepherd admission policy in the gateway that queries the arbiter with a compact request context and receives an Action {ADMIT, SOFT_DEMOTE_TO_MODEL=xyz, REROUTE_REGION=eu-west-1, REJECT}. The arbiter maintains a tiny token-escrow per active tenant (TTL=30s) to allow short bursts and to prevent immediate hard rejections.

Key algorithms: predictive smoothing uses EWMA over per-tenant token burn rate with decay tuned by plan class. Soft-demote scoring factors: plan_priority_weight, token_balance_ratio, regional_latency_cost, variant_compatibility_score, and recent_error_rate. A configurable policy graph defines thresholds for demotion vs reject.

Data flows and caches: billing/credits are asynchronously synced from the canonical quota DB and sharded into Redis clusters per region for low-latency reads. Arbiter is stateless for horizontal scaling but writes short-lived token-escrow entries back to Redis. The gateway caches arbiter decisions for identical prefixes for up to 50ms to reduce QPS to the arbiter for high-throughput burst windows.
implementation_steps: Add Redis-backed token-escrow schema and migrations (storage team collaboration)
Implement arbiter gRPC API: Evaluate(request_context) -> action+reason+meta
Add EWMA-based smoothing module with per-plan parameters (config driven)
Integrate gateway call-site: synchronous call with 300µs timeout and local cache of 50ms
Implement model-variant registry lookup and variant compatibility scoring
Create Console toggles and rollout flags for canary control
Add tracing tags and dashboard panels (per-decision breakdown)
rollout_plan: Dev: unit tests + integration tests in local cluster (branch feature-toggle=true)
Staging: enable for 10% of traffic in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 for 48h; monitor error, latency, decision distribution
Canary: 1% production traffic with auto-promote to 10% over 3 hours if error rate <0.2% and latency SLOs met
Full: region-by-region (start with eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 -> ap-southeast-1) with 2-hour observation gates
Rollback: flip feature flag off and clear token-escrow cache if decision error spike >1% or median latency regression >10%
tests: Unit: smoothing math, edge-case token underflow, action selection
Integration: arbiter+gateway loop with Redis emulator
Perf: synthetic mixed-tier workload that simulates plan bursts (10k req/s) to validate arbiter P95 <500µs
Chaos: simulate Redis partial failure and validate gateway fallback to conservative local policy
Regression: end-to-end quality eval on a held-out prompt set comparing primary vs fallback variants
risks: Risk of incorrect demotion causing quality regressions for low-tier customers; mitigated via conservative thresholds and eval hooks
Redis availability increases blast radius for token-escrow; mitigation: local gateway fallback and short TTLs
Billing/Quota sync lag could cause stale admits; mitigation: add grace buffer and conservative under-admit defaults
